transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Orion Head of ML), Rajesh Iyer (Orion CTO), Marta Gomez (Orion Data Eng)

Auto-summary: discuss open-model shortlist for POC, success criteria (accuracy/intent-precision, latency <= 400ms p50, cost targets), workload sizing (100 qps peak, 20k daily active users), benchmark plan and timeline.

Topics:
- Success criteria and metrics
- Workload sizing and expected QPS
- Benchmark matrix (models, quantization, sequence lengths)
- Security/residency/VPC requirements
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intros we got about 50 minutes. Diego and I will run through the POC plan. Lena, Rajesh, you good to start?
[00:12] Lena: Yeah thanks, um quick context, we are building a multilingual support assistant, English, Spanish, Portuguese at launch, some internal Spanish-only workflows too. Our main goals are high intent accuracy for routing and short latencies, so customers don't wait.
[00:28] Rajesh: The infra constraint is we need data residency in eu-west for EU users and SOC2 is non-negotiable. We'll evaluate hosting options - hosted API vs dedicated in our VPC.
[00:40] Diego: Got it. For the POC we usually recommended we run a bench matrix across 3-4 open models: a high-quality large model, a mid-size multitask model, and a low-cost trimmed variant. Thinking Falcon 40B v2 (high quality), Mistral 8x (cost/perf sweet spot), and MPT-30B or Vicuna 13B trimmed for cheaper fallbacks.
[01:05] Lena: Are these all supported on Redwood Dedicated & Private? Our security team will want an on-prem or VPC deploy if pricing requires it.
[01:12] Samira: Yes - Redwood Dedicated supports all those; Redwood Private can run in your VPC or on-prem with our private control plane and KMS integration. We can provide SOC2 docs and the deployment checklist.
[01:25] Marta: Quick question on latency: our internal SLA target is p50 < 400ms for short queries (~64 tokens). Can Falcon 40B hit that in dedicated?
[01:36] Diego: On well-configured A100/H100 pools we see sub-300ms p50 for 64-token sequences with batching tuned and KV cache warm. If you quantize to int8 or use Triton kernels we can get further improvements. But bigger context windows and RAG will bump latency.
[01:50] Rajesh: What about cost? We can't have every request on a 40B running all the time.
[01:56] Diego: Typical approach: prefix caching + routing. 60-70% of requests hit small context or cached responses so you can route warm prefixes to smaller models. For POC we'll run an apples-to-apples token-cost comparison across models (token/sec and $/k tokens).
[02:12] Lena: Success criteria - what should we measure?
[02:15] Samira: We suggest quantifiable goals: intent accuracy >= 90% on your labeled set, avg response time p50 <= 400ms and p95 < 1s for the 64-token baseline, cost target <$0.002 per user request averaged (we'll refine). Also operational: ability to run in eu-west VPC and pass SOC2 checklist.
[02:39] Marta: For datasets I can share two sets: 1) 5k recent support transcripts (sanitized) and 2) 1k multi-turn escalation cases. Will that work?
[02:48] Diego: Perfect, that'll let us test both short-hand intents and longer context. Please include language labels.
[02:54] Lena: We also need multilingual evals - are there models better at Spanish/Portuguese?
[02:59] Diego: Mistral performs well across languages but Falcon 40B v2 is still strong. We can include an LLM fine-tuned on multilingual data, like a Vicuna variant, to compare. Also MPT-30B with tokenizer tweaks sometimes helps in Portuguese.
[03:17] Rajesh: Timeline? We want a decision by end of June to start pilot in July.
[03:21] Samira: For that timeline we recommend: you send datasets by 6/16, we run initial benchmarks 6/17-6/19, deliver a short report by 6/22, then we sync to define pilot configuration. That gets you to July pilot start.
[03:36] Lena: Sounds good. For the bench matrix can you spell out model/config variants?
[03:40] Diego: Sure - the proposed matrix: Falcon 40B v2 (fp16, int8 quant maybe), Mistral 8x (fp16), MPT-30B (fp16), Vicuna 13B trimmed (fast low-cost variant). For each model we'll test: 1) baseline 64-token seq, 2) 256-token RAG scenario, 3) quantized int8 where supported. Metrics: accuracy/intent F1, hallucination rate (manual sample), latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost/k tokens.
[04:06] Lena: Any gotchas around tokenization or evaluation scripts? We have some internal scoring; can we share a scoring notebook?
[04:12] Diego: Yes please. We'll adapt your scripts to the bench harness. Ideally provide a Jupyter notebook and a small scoring function; otherwise we'll port.
[04:20] Marta: Network - if we run Dedicated in our VPC, how does initial onboarding look? We need SSO, SAML for access and KMS for keys.
[04:29] Samira: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. For Private deployments we can do customer-managed KMS. We'll send the setup checklist after the call.
[04:38] Rajesh: Competitors we're evaluating: OpenAI hosted for fast time-to-value and Anthropic for safety. How do you compare?
[04:47] Samira: Hosted is fastest to get started; Redwood adds observability and dedicated options for predictable cost. From safety standpoint we can run safety evals and integrate reranking or filtering. For the POC we'll show apples-to-apples latency/cost and quality.
[04:59] Diego: One more note: for the multilingual intents it's worth testing lower-parameter models tuned on multilingual corpora because sometimes they generalize better than zero-shot Llama variants. We'll include that in the matrix.
[05:12] Lena: Great. Any blockers on our side?
[05:15] Samira: Datasets and an infra contact for networking - Marta will be the owner for S3 share and Rajesh for VPC decisions.
[05:23] Marta: I can be infra owner, I'll open a temporary S3 bucket and share creds with Diego.
[05:29] Diego: Awesome. I'll put together the benchmark yaml and share. Samira will follow up on pricing.
[05:35] Samira: Recap of next steps: Diego sends benchmark config, Samira sends pricing and SOC2 docs, Lena uploads datasets, schedule bench run 6/17.
[05:45] Rajesh: We may want a short technical deep dive on the 17th if we hit infra or kernel tuning issues.
[05:51] Samira: We'll block time - Diego you okay to lead that deep dive?
[05:54] Diego: Yep.
[05:56] Samira: Great thank you everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the checklist.

End of transcript.
